title: Returnship & Internal Mobility: Reboarding, Role Transfers, and Talent Recapture
author: Aisha Rahman
content:
Overview:
This document defines Redwood's program and operational process for returnships (re-hiring former employees), internal mobility (role transfers and promotions between teams), and related reboarding practices. It provides eligibility criteria, step-by-step workflows, manager and People Ops responsibilities, templates, and metrics we track to ensure fast, fair, and inclusive moves.

Goals and guiding principles:
- Reduce friction for internal moves and returning alumni while preserving role-fit and calibration.
- Make decisions within predictable SLAs and with transparent candidate experience.
- Preserve institutional knowledge and accelerate time-to-impact for returnees.
- Ensure equitable access to opportunities across levels, functions, and demographics.

Scope:
Applies to:
- Former Redwood employees who left in good standing and reapply or are invited back ("returnships").
- Active Redwood employees applying to open roles in other teams (internal mobility).
- Transfers initiated by managers for operational redeployments.

Definitions:
- Returnship: Re-hire pathway for alumni; may include shortened interviewing and a tailored reboarding plan.
- Reboarding: The onboarding process adapted for returnees or internal transferees, focusing on changed systems, policy updates, and team reintegration.
- Internal mobility: Any approved lateral or vertical move of an active employee between teams or roles.

Eligibility and guardrails (hard rules):
1) Returnship eligibility:
   - Candidate left in good standing (no unresolved disciplinary actions).
   - Minimum 30 days since separation for reapplication unless exception approved by VP People.
   - No return if separation was due to security incidents or data breaches.
2) Internal transfers:
   - Must have manager conversation before applying.
   - Compensation/leveling changes must be reviewed by Compensation Partner.
3) Exceptions process: exceptions are documented and require People Ops + Hiring Manager + Head of Function sign-off.

Primary owners and contacts:
- Program lead: Marcus Lee (Talent Partner) — overall SLA tracking and program escalation.
- People Ops intake: returnship@redwood.ai — initial eligibility checks.
- Compensation partner: Priya Desai — leveling and comp approvals.
- VP People: Clara Zhang — final exception approvals.

Process flows (high-level):
A) Returnship (fast-track) workflow:
   1. Referral / application received by Talent Partner. (Owner: Talent Partner).
   2. Eligibility screen (People Ops): verify separation reason, employment history, and rehire window. SLA: 5 business days.
   3. Hiring manager screening call (30 minutes) — focus on role changes and expectation alignment. SLA: schedule within 7 business days.
   4. Targeted interview loop (1-2 interviews max for fast-track): emphasis on current role fit and ramp plan.
   5. Decision and offer: standard offer except: tenure-based benefits reset defined below.
   6. Reboarding kickoff: 30–60–90 plan tailored to role and time away.

B) Internal mobility (standard) workflow:
   1. Candidate notifies current manager and submits internal transfer request in Workday.
   2. Hiring manager conducts initial screen and submits interview plan to People Ops.
   3. Interview loop conducted with at least one cross-functional interviewer.
   4. Compensation & leveling review occurs before offers. SLA: 10 business days for comp review.
   5. Offer accepted -> transfer start date agreed with both managers.

Detailed step-by-step checklist (numbered):
1. Pre-application manager conversation (active employees only). Document in the candidate's internal transfer form.
2. Intake form (People Ops) collects: previous manager, last role, reason for move, target role, relocation requirements.
3. Interview plan must include at least one behavioral and one role-specific assessment. If role is senior (L7+), include a calibration interview with the function lead.
4. Compensation team completes leveling check and proposed salary/career mapping.
5. Manager-to-manager transition plan: knowledge-transfer sessions (minimum 5 hours for IC roles, 10 hours for senior IC/manager roles).
6. Reboarding meeting scheduled for day 1 with People Ops and new manager.

Table: SLA matrix:
| Milestone | Owner | SLA | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Eligibility screen (returnship) | People Ops | 5 business days | Automatic fail -> escalate to Talent Partner |
| Hiring manager initial screen | Hiring Manager | 7 business days | If not scheduled, People Ops will follow up after 10 business days |
| Compensation review (internal move) | Compensation Partner | 10 business days | Includes leveling, sign-on review, and budget check |
| Final offer decision | Hiring Manager + People Ops | 3 business days | Time from last interview to written offer |

Reboarding: 30-60-90 template (for returnees and transferees)
- Day 0 (pre-start): IT access checklist, benefits enrollment update, manager intro email, workspace setup.
- Week 1 (0–7 days): Team orientation, product overview, immediate blockers/OKRs, buddy assigned.
- Month 1 (0–30 days): Deliverable: first small ticket or onboarding project; weekly 1:1 cadence with manager.
- Month 2 (31–60 days): Cross-team introductions; performance objectives drafted; feedback checkpoint.
- Month 3 (61–90 days): Full role responsibilities; probation review (if applicable); career mapping conversation.

Manager responsibilities checklist (quick):
- Confirm candidate eligibility and discuss plan with People Ops.
- Prepare role-specific onboarding materials and knowledge-transfer schedule.
- Assign a buddy and ensure initial 30-day goals are clear.
- Complete manager acceptance form in HRIS within 2 business days of offer acceptance.

People Ops responsibilities checklist:
- Run eligibility check and track SLAs.
- Coordinate interviews and compensation review.
- Prepare reboarding packet (policy changes since their last tenure).
- Log the move in the internal mobility dashboard and update retention metrics.

Compensation, benefits, and tenure considerations:
- Benefits re-enrollment: returnees are eligible for benefits on the standard New Hire schedule unless otherwise specified in offer.
- Tenure and vacation: prior tenure is credited for service awards and vesting schedules in most cases; exceptions documented in the offer.
- Sign-on bonuses: allowed only with Comp partner approval and documented business case.

Interview differences and calibration notes for returnships:
- Focus less on historical organizational fit and more on current technical/business fit.
- Use a "time-away" interview question set to assess learning and risk areas (sample questions provided in Appendix A).
- Calibration: hiring managers must include at least one interviewer who was not on the original team to avoid halo/bias effects.

Reporting and metrics (monthly):
- Time-to-decision (returnship): median target <= 12 business days.
- Acceptance rate (returnee offers): target >= 75%.
- Internal mobility retention at 12 months: target >= 85%.
- Percentage of moves processed within SLA: target >= 90%.

Privacy and data handling:
- Returnee background materials are handled per HR privacy policy.
- Personal pay history will only be accessed by Compensation Partner and anonymized in reports.

Related templates and appendices:
- Appendix A: Time-away interview question bank (link: /confluence/people-ops/time-away-interview-bank).
- Appendix B: Reboarding packet checklist (link: /confluence/people-ops/reboarding-packet-template).
- Appendix C: Internal mobility intake form (Workday) — sample payload included.

Escalation and exceptions:
- If SLAs are missed twice in a rolling 90-day period for a given team, People Ops will trigger a process review with the hiring manager's lead.
- Security or legal flags during eligibility require pause and review with Security and Legal teams.

Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: Does prior tenure always count for vesting?
A: Generally yes, but vesting credit is reviewed on a case-by-case basis and stated in the return offer.

Q: Can a returnee bypass interviews entirely?
A: Only under a documented fast-track for critical roles with approval from VP People and Talent Partner.
